Depressometer — a playful mood scanner. Not a medical device.

Depressometer is a playful, camera-based mood scanner. It is NOT a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, or measure depression.

The score blends facial cues that appear in depression research: smile intensity (action units AU12/AU6), eye openness (an Eye-Aspect-Ratio style alertness cue), head movement (a psychomotor-retardation proxy) and facial expressivity. Sources: Girard & Cohn (ACII 2009); Jones et al. (2018); FacePsy (2024).

⚠️ "Smiling depression" is real, so a smile never dictates the score on its own.

PRIVACY: All face processing happens on-device using Google ML Kit. Camera frames are analysed in memory and discarded immediately — no images are stored, uploaded, or shared. Only the numeric score and its level are saved, in a private local file on your phone.

If you are struggling, please talk to someone you trust or a qualified professional.

string-array.name: affirmations
string-array.item: You\'re glowing today — that good energy is yours to keep. 🌟
Your face is carrying real warmth right now. Nice. ✨
Steady and balanced — a solid place to be. 🌤️
A softer day, and that\'s okay. You\'re doing better than you feel. 💙
Hard moments never tell the whole story. You matter, and this passes. 💙

string-array.name: tips_cheerful
string-array.item: Keep doing what you\'re doing — it\'s working.
Bank this win: note one thing that made today good.
Share the energy — tell someone you appreciate them.

string-array.name: tips_happy
string-array.item: A short walk or stretch keeps the good mood rolling.
Hydrate — low energy often just means low water.
Message a friend; connection lifts mood fast.

string-array.name: tips_neutral
string-array.item: Step outside for 10 minutes of daylight.
Try 5 slow breaths: in 4s, hold 4s, out 4s.
Put on one song you love and actually listen to it.
Drink a glass of water and roll your shoulders.

string-array.name: tips_blue
string-array.item: Reach out to one person today — a call or a text.
Move your body for 15 minutes (walk, dance, anything).
Cut back on doomscrolling for the next hour.
Get some sunlight and eat a proper meal.

string-array.name: tips_high
string-array.item: Talk to someone you trust today — you don\'t have to carry it alone.
One small step: water, an open window, a step outside.
If this feeling lingers, a real check-in with a professional can help.
